headline: Light weekend rain and fog, then a wetter, windier pattern settles in next week.
summary: A ridge of high pressure, an area of settled, stable air, is moving inland, leaving Western Washington cool and foggy this morning, with some freezing fog possible. A low pressure system dropping south from the northeast Pacific will sit just offshore through Sunday, bringing light rain and snow in the mountains and highs mostly in the 40s and 50s. A stronger low forming offshore early next week will make the pattern much more active through the end of the week. Expect repeated rounds of lowland rain, mountain snow, and gusty winds, with high surf and a growing risk of minor coastal flooding around high tides. Forecasters are fairly confident about the quiet weekend and the busier stretch ahead, but the timing and strength of individual systems, and how strong the winds get, are less certain. The Skokomish River may reach flood stage late in the week.
